title: Numbers and strings
objective: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to do maths in Python, join and measure strings, and convert between numbers and text.

sections.title: Doing maths
sections.text: Python uses + to add, - to subtract, * to multiply and / to divide. Dividing with / always gives a float, so 6 / 2 is 3.0 and 7 / 2 is 3.5.

sections.title: Whole division and remainders
sections.text: // divides and keeps only the whole number part, so 7 // 2 is 3. % gives the remainder, so 7 % 2 is 1. A number is even when number % 2 is 0.

sections.title: Joining and measuring strings
sections.text: + joins two strings together: "Hi " + "Sam" makes "Hi Sam". len("Sam") counts the characters, so it gives 3. An f-string puts values straight into text: f"I am {age}" puts the value of age where {age} is.

sections.title: Changing types
sections.text: Python will not join a string and a number with +. "Age: " + 12 gives a TypeError. str(12) turns a number into the text "12", and int("12") turns text into the number 12.

examples.title: Example 1: Four ways to divide and add
Example 2: Working with text
examples.code:
name = "Zara"
age = 13
print("Hi " + name)
print(len(name))
print(f"{name} is {age} years old.")
print(int("5") + 1)
examples.output:
Hi Zara
4
Zara is 13 years old.
6

check_questions.explanation: 5 goes into 17 three whole times (15), and 2 is left over. % gives what is left over.

misconception.1: 3 is how many whole times 5 fits, which is 17 // 5.
misconception.3: % is not subtraction. It gives the remainder.

check_questions.explanation: Both values are in quotes, so they are strings. + joins strings together.

misconception.0: The quotes make these text, so + joins them instead of adding.
misconception.1: + joins strings with no space between them.
misconception.2: Joining two strings is fine. The error only happens when you mix a string and a number.

check_questions.prompt: This code gives an error. Which line prints Points: 10 without an error?
check_questions.explanation: An f-string puts the value of points into the text, so it prints Points: 10.

misconception.0: points is already an int. You need to turn it into text, not into a number.
misconception.1: This prints the word points, not the number 10.
misconception.3: Text must go inside quotes, so this is a syntax error.

try_it.title: Try It Yourself
try_it.instructions: Change the values of a and b and see what //, % and / give. Then change the last line so it prints a sentence about you.
try_it.starter:
a = 20
b = 6
print(a // b)
print(a % b)
print(a / b)
print(f"{a} sweets shared by {b} people is {a // b} each, with {a % b} left over.")
